Well, that's the weird thing. When I'm not feeling so heavy and down, my sleep is... well, it's still messed up, but in a totally different way. Like, a few weeks ago, before this really bad slump hit, I wasn't sad at all. Actually, I felt pretty great. But my sleep was still completely off.

Normally, if I get three hours of sleep, I'm dragging. I need, like, a venti dark roast from Starbucks just to function. But during that time? I felt completely charged. I felt like I had electricity humming under my skin. I didn't even need coffee. I'd just bounce into the office, ready to tackle the spreadsheets, talking a mile a minute to the receptionist. So yeah, when I'm not feeling sad, my sleep doesn't really get *better*, it just changes from this awful, heavy insomnia to this weird state where I barely sleep at all but feel like I have all the energy in the world. Well, it's not always... I mean, mostly, yeah, when I'm not in that awful, heavy place, I do tend to have a lot of energy. But sometimes it's more than just energy, it's like this intense drive to *do* things. 

Like, during that same time a few weeks ago, when I was only sleeping those three or four hours? I wasn't just reorganizing the kitchen. I was doing everything. I would get home from work—and keep in mind, I'd been doing bookkeeping for eight hours straight, staring at numbers, which usually leaves me completely fried—but I'd walk in the door and it was like a switch flipped. I'd start deep cleaning the bathroom, scrubbing the grout with a toothbrush. And then while the floor was drying, I'd sit at my laptop and start making these massive, incredibly detailed lists for renovating the condo. Like, pulling up Home Depot tabs, comparing the prices of brushed nickel versus matte black hardware for the cabinets, mapping out a whole budget on a spreadsheet. 

And then, I don't even know how, but that led me down this rabbit hole of checking mortgage interest rates, just in case I wanted to refinance, even though I just bought the place. I was reading all these financial blogs and calculating amortization schedules at like 11:30 at night. And *then*, because I was thinking about money, I decided I needed a side hustle. So I started outlining a business plan for doing freelance bookkeeping for small businesses in the area. I was looking up domain names, drafting cold emails to send to local coffee shops and boutiques... I mean, I was just going and going and going. It was like I had a motor inside me that I couldn't shut off. I just felt this absolute need to be productive, to fix things, to plan things, to start new projects. So yeah, I guess when I'm not sad, I don't just have energy... I have this crazy burst of activity where I feel like I can take on the entire world, all at once, usually after I've already worked a full day.

It's definitely in distinct episodes. It's not like a constant baseline thing. Like, when I'm just feeling normal—which honestly feels like a luxury these days—I'm just... normal. I go to work, I come home, I watch some TV, I go to bed. But these periods, like the one earlier in the month, they're like a switch gets flipped, you know? But the thing is, it wasn't just all positive, productive energy. It's like... because I felt so fast and so capable, everyone else felt like they were moving in slow motion, and it would just drive me crazy. I'd be in this unstoppable zone, and then my mom would call to ask me something totally mundane, like what time she should bring her car to the mechanic, and I would just snap at her. Like, really bite her head off. I'd be like, "Mom, I don't know, just look at the hours online, I'm busy!" And normally, I'd never talk to her like that. We have a good relationship. 

Or at work—I was doing my bookkeeping, flying through the spreadsheets, and my supervisor came over to ask a really simple question about one of the accounts. Something she asks me all the time, totally standard procedure. And I just felt this flash of pure annoyance, like, hot prickly irritation all over my neck. I had to bite my tongue so hard not to yell at her for interrupting my flow. I ended up giving her this really clipped, short answer, and she kind of looked at me weird and walked away. It's like, when I'm in one of those episodes, I'm so revved up that any little roadblock or question that wouldn't normally bother me at all just feels like this massive, infuriating obstacle. So yeah, it's definitely an episode, and it's not just energy... it's like this intense, impatient, irritable drive that just takes over for a while until I crash back down into that awful heavy feeling.

========== OUTPUT [patient] ==========
Well, it's like... you know how a balloon looks when you let all the air out of it at once? It just kind of flops to the floor, completely deflated. That's exactly what happens to me. The motor just... dies. 

One day I'm alphabetizing the spices and drafting business plans, and then literally the next morning, or maybe a couple days later, I just wake up and it's gone. The energy is completely wiped out. And it's not just that I'm tired from not sleeping during that whole hyper phase, though I guess that's probably part of the physical side of it, but it's this mood shift that is just so drastic and overwhelming. 

Lately, when that crash happens, I wake up with this incredibly heavy, empty feeling. It's like someone poured lead into my veins overnight. I can't even explain how heavy my limbs feel. And the sadness is just... it's everywhere. I'll just be sitting there in my living room, looking around at my condo... and you have to understand, I worked *so* hard to buy this place. I started working right out of high school, doing data entry, working my way up to the bookkeeping position I have now, just saving every single penny I could so I wouldn't have to rent forever. I should be so proud of it, right? I mean, I *am* proud of it, normally. 

But when I'm in this awful slump, I'll just be sitting on the couch I saved up for, in this beautiful condo that I worked so hard for, and it just makes me want to cry. I'll just look at the walls and feel absolutely nothing but this crushing sadness. It doesn't make any rational sense. Why would I want to cry looking at my own biggest achievement? But I do. The tears just sit there behind my eyes all day. I can barely drag myself into the kitchen that I was just scrubbing with a toothbrush a week prior. It's just this dark, heavy cloud that settles over everything, and the emptiness is almost worse than the sadness, if that makes sense? Because when I was up, everything mattered *so* much, and then suddenly, absolutely nothing matters at all. I'll just sit there, staring at the brushed nickel cabinet hardware I spent three hours picking out online, and just... cry. It's just so exhausting to go from feeling like I own the world to feeling like I can't even exist in my own living room.

Well, lately, yeah. I mean, it feels like it's always that way right now. This... this really obvious cycling between that crazy, charged-up stretch and then this awful, heavy crash... it's been going on for about a month now. Basically ever since the mortgage actually became real.

It's just been a solid month of this really obvious bouncing back and forth, up and down, and it's just... I don't even know which version of me is going to wake up in the morning anymore. I mean, I guess I've always had days where I'm more tired than others, but this specific pattern? Going from being totally unstoppable to just completely hollowed out? That's been the last month, exactly since that piece of mail showed up and the house became this real, permanent thing. It’s exhausting, honestly, just going from one extreme to the other like this.

I'm either staring at the ceiling for hours because my thoughts won't stop, or I'm up before the sun feeling totally drained, and I just don't know how to fix it on my own anymore.\n\nDoctor: Do you find yourself worrying excessively about everyday things, not just work-related tasks like bookkeeping?\n\nPatient: Um... no, not really. I mean, it's not like I'm sitting there fretting about, you know, whether I left the stove on, or if my car is going to break down, or what I'm going to make for dinner on Thursday. My mom is a huge worrier, she worries about literally everything—like if the mailman is ten minutes late she thinks something terrible happened—but I'm really not like that at all. \n\nIt's less about *worrying* and more just... noise? Like, even with the bookkeeping stuff I mentioned, when I'm laying there, it's not that I'm anxious or stressed about the invoices. It's just that I'm *thinking* about them. Like I can literally picture the Excel cells and the formulas in my head. Or, I don't know, I'll think about a movie I watched three weeks ago and try to remember the lead actor's name, and then I'll think about what else that actor was in, and then I'm thinking about the popcorn I ate at the theater, and then I'm wondering how popcorn is actually harvested... it's just this endless chain of completely random stuff. \n\nSo, no, I wouldn't say I'm worrying about everyday things. I mean, I pay my rent, I go to work, I get my groceries, and none of that really stresses me out or makes me bite my nails or anything. My brain is just more like a television flipping through channels really, really fast. But it's not like a scary channel, you know? Just... loud. And it just won't turn off.\n\nDoctor: Have you been feeling sad or down lately?\n\nPatient: Yeah... yeah, I have. Um, it's actually been really bad lately. Like, I'll wake up—when I do manage to sleep, or when I wake up at 4 AM like I was saying—and I just have this... this incredibly heavy feeling right in the center of my chest. It's almost like a physical weight, you know? And it's just this deep, deep emptiness. \n\nLike, I live in this little condo, right? And I worked *so* hard to get it. I saved up for years from my bookkeeping job, I scrimped and saved, I didn't go out with friends so I could put away a down payment, and I finally got this place. I picked out the paint colors, I bought this really nice rug for the living room... I should be so happy there. It's my own space. But lately, I'll just be sitting on my couch, looking around at this place I practically killed myself to get, and I just feel... nothing. Or worse than nothing. I just sit there and I want to cry. \n\nAnd I don't even know *why* I want to cry. It's not like anything terrible happened that day. I just feel so incredibly down and drained, like all the color has just been washed out of everything. I'll just sit there staring at the wall, and the tears will just start welling up, and I just feel so sad and heavy and... just completely empty inside, even when I'm surrounded by all the things I worked so hard for. It's really awful. It's like I can't even enjoy my own life right now.\n\nDoctor: Do you find that your sleep gets better or worse when you're feeling less sad?\n\nPatient: Well, that's the weird thing. When I'm not feeling so heavy and down, my sleep is... well, it's still messed up, but in a totally different way. Like, a few weeks ago, before this really bad slump hit, I wasn't sad at all. Actually, I felt pretty great. But my sleep was still completely off. \n\nThe difference was, I wasn't lying there staring at the ceiling feeling drained, or waking up at 4 AM feeling like a zombie. I was just... not sleeping much at all, and I didn't even care. There were several nights in a row where I think I only slept maybe three or four hours total. I'd go to bed at like 2 AM because I was busy reorganizing my entire kitchen—like, taking everything out of the cabinets, wiping down the shelves, putting down new contact paper, alphabetizing my spices, the whole nine yards. And then my alarm would go off at 6 AM for work, and I'd just pop right out of bed. \n\nNormally, if I get three hours of sleep, I'm dragging. I need, like, a venti dark roast from Starbucks just to function. But during that time? I felt completely charged. I felt like I had electricity humming under my skin. I didn't even need coffee. I'd just bounce into the office, ready to tackle the spreadsheets, talking a mile a minute to the receptionist. So yeah, when I'm not feeling sad, my sleep doesn't really get *better*, it just changes from this awful, heavy insomnia to this weird state where I barely sleep at all but feel like I have all the energy in the world. It's like my body forgets it actually needs rest.\n\nDoctor: Do you always feel like you have a lot of energy when you're not feeling sad?\n\nPatient: Well, it's not always... I mean, mostly, yeah, when I'm not in that awful, heavy place, I do tend to have a lot of energy. But sometimes it's more than just energy, it's like this intense drive to *do* things. \n\nLike, during that same time a few weeks ago, when I was only sleeping those three or four hours? I wasn't just reorganizing the kitchen. I was doing everything. I would get home from work—and keep in mind, I'd been doing bookkeeping for eight hours straight, staring at numbers, which usually leaves me completely fried—but I'd walk in the door and it was like a switch flipped. I'd start deep cleaning the bathroom, scrubbing the grout with a toothbrush. And then while the floor was drying, I'd sit at my laptop and start making these massive, incredibly detailed lists for renovating the condo. Like, pulling up Home Depot tabs, comparing the prices of brushed nickel versus matte black hardware for the cabinets, mapping out a whole budget on a spreadsheet. \n\nAnd then, I don't even know how, but that led me down this rabbit hole of checking mortgage interest rates, just in case I wanted to refinance, even though I just bought the place. I was reading all these financial blogs and calculating amortization schedules at like 11:30 at night. And *then*, because I was thinking about money, I decided I needed a side hustle. So I started outlining a business plan for doing freelance bookkeeping for small businesses in the area. I was looking up domain names, drafting cold emails to send to local coffee shops and boutiques... I mean, I was just going and going and going. It was like I had a motor inside me that I couldn't shut off. I just felt this absolute need to be productive, to fix things, to plan things, to start new projects. So yeah, I guess when I'm not sad, I don't just have energy... I have this crazy burst of activity where I feel like I can take on the entire world, all at once, usually after I've already worked a full day.\n\nDoctor: Do these periods of having a lot of energy and wanting to take on a lot of projects happen in distinct episodes, or is it more of a constant state when you're not feeling sad?\n\nPatient: It's definitely in distinct episodes. It's not like a constant baseline thing. Like, when I'm just feeling normal—which honestly feels like a luxury these days—I'm just... normal. I go to work, I come home, I watch some TV, I go to bed. But these periods, like the one earlier in the month, they're like a switch gets flipped, you know? It's like a wave that just washes over me. \n\nEarlier in the month, it was exactly like that. I just woke up one day and felt almost... lit up. Like I was glowing from the inside out, and I felt completely unstoppable. Like every idea I had was brilliant and I had to execute it right that second. The kitchen, the business plan, the refinancing... it all felt so urgent and exciting. \n\nBut the thing is, it wasn't just all positive, productive energy. It's like... because I felt so fast and so capable, everyone else felt like they were moving in slow motion, and it would just drive me crazy. I'd be in this unstoppable zone, and then my mom would call to ask me something totally mundane, like what time she should bring her car to the mechanic, and I would just snap at her. Like, really bite her head off. I'd be like, \"Mom, I don't know, just look at the hours online, I'm busy!\" And normally, I'd never talk to her like that. We have a good relationship. \n\nOr at work—I was doing my bookkeeping, flying through the spreadsheets, and my supervisor came over to ask a really simple question about one of the accounts. Something she asks me all the time, totally standard procedure. And I just felt this flash of pure annoyance, like, hot prickly irritation all over my neck. I had to bite my tongue so hard not to yell at her for interrupting my flow. I ended up giving her this really clipped, short answer, and she kind of looked at me weird and walked away. It's like, when I'm in one of those episodes, I'm so revved up that any little roadblock or question that wouldn't normally bother me at all just feels like this massive, infuriating obstacle. So yeah, it's definitely an episode, and it's not just energy... it's like this intense, impatient, irritable drive that just takes over for a while until I crash back down into that awful heavy feeling.\n\nDoctor: What happens to your mood and energy level after one of these episodes of feeling unstoppable and irritable ends?\n\nPatient: Well, it's like... you know how a balloon looks when you let all the air out of it at once? The motor just... dies. \n\nOne day I'm alphabetizing the spices and drafting business plans, and then literally the next morning, or maybe a couple days later, I just wake up and it's gone. The energy is completely wiped out. And it's not just that I'm tired from not sleeping during that whole hyper phase, though I guess that's probably part of the physical side of it, but it's this mood shift that is just so drastic and overwhelming. \n\nLately, when that crash happens, I wake up with this incredibly heavy, empty feeling. It's like someone poured lead into my veins overnight. I can't even explain how heavy my limbs feel. And the sadness is just... it's everywhere. I started working right out of high school, doing data entry, working my way up to the bookkeeping position I have now, just saving every single penny I could so I wouldn't have to rent forever. Because when I was up, everything mattered *so* much, and then suddenly, absolutely nothing matters at all. I'll just sit there, staring at the brushed nickel cabinet hardware I spent three hours picking out online, and just... cry. It's just so exhausting to go from feeling like I own the world to feeling like I can't even exist in my own living room.\n\nDoctor: Do you always feel sad or empty after one of these episodes of high energy and irritability ends?\n\nPatient: Well, lately, yeah.
